$NVDA  - SEC INVESTIGATING NVIDIA OVER POTENTIAL ACCOUNTING ISSUES 

The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is examining Nvidia's accounting practices, Reuters reports, citing two people familiar with the confidential investigation.

The probe adds to mounting legal pressure following the company's leadership scandal and ongoing scrutiny of AI chip exports to China.

Separately, the Justice Department is reviewing Nvidia's $12.9 billion Hugging Face acquisition as part of a broader antitrust investigation.

The SEC's specific accounting concerns remain unclear, and no wrongdoing has been established.

Nvidia has not publicly commented on the latest allegations.

U.S. AND QATAR HOLD TALKS TO REVIVE IRAN CEASEFIRE — AXIOS

Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met senior Qatari officials in Berlin on Thursday to discuss restarting U.S.-Iran negotiations, Axios reports.

Qatar is seeking to restore the ceasefire, resume nuclear talks and prevent renewed military escalation.

President Trump said Friday that Iran wants a deal, but not one he considers acceptable.

Trump has indicated he will delay a decision on further military action until 2027.

Despite intensified diplomatic efforts, no significant breakthrough has been reported.
(@WalterBloomberg)

$NVDA  - SUSPECTED CHINESE SPY'S CHIP NETWORK LINKED TO MILITARY SUPPLIERS — NYT

Alice Huang, a figure in the Nvidia scandal, has extensive family and business ties to Chinese defense contractors, according to The New York Times and intelligence firm Strider Technologies.

The investigation traced approximately $3.6 billion in Chinese government funding through companies associated with Huang's network.

The companies reportedly supplied Nvidia-powered infrastructure and maintained links to contractors involved in Chinese military aircraft, radar and missile systems.

Nvidia sought licenses to ship over 40,000 H200 chips to a company linked to the network but says it never shipped them.

No evidence establishes that Nvidia chips ultimately supported Chinese military projects.
(@WalterBloomberg)

$ANT - WILLIAM BLAIR SAYS ANTHROPIC AT $83 WOULD TRADE AT A DISCOUNT

William Blair analysts, led by Arjun Bhatia, argue that Anthropic's $83 IPO price represents an attractive valuation as shares retreat toward that level.

At $83, Anthropic trades at approximately 9x projected 2027 revenue of $136 billion on an enterprise-value basis.

For comparison, Meta trades near 5x revenue, while CrowdStrike trades around 36x.

William Blair calls Anthropic's multiple "very reasonable", citing significantly faster growth than many established technology companies.

2027 revenue consensus ranges from $130 billion to $139 billion, according to FactSet and Visible Alpha.

$NVDA $AMD - TOP REPUBLICAN SENATOR ACCUSES COMMERCE SECRETARY OF IGNORING CHINA CHIP WARNINGS

Senate Intelligence Committee Chairman Tom Cotton says Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick repeatedly ignored warnings about potential AI chip smuggling to China.

Cotton specifically cited concerns about Megaspeed, a company linked to the ongoing Nvidia investigation.

According to the report, Commerce approved exports of more than 800,000 Nvidia and AMD chips to China through May 11.

Nvidia maintains its shipments were legally authorized.

Cotton expects Congress to pursue stricter semiconductor export controls, potentially including chip-tracking requirements and restrictions on advanced manufacturing equipment.

The allegations intensify scrutiny of U.S. technology exports and the Commerce Department's oversight.

FED'S COOK CALLS FOR TIGHTER MONETARY POLICY, WARNS INFLATION RISKS ARE GROWING

Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned that current interest rates are not restrictive enough to bring inflation under control.

Cook said September's rate hike was insufficient and that delaying further tightening risks embedding inflation, potentially requiring more aggressive action later.

She described financial conditions as too accommodative, while characterizing economic growth as strong and the labor market as healthy.

Cook added that tariff-related inflation pressures have faded and sees little evidence that AI is significantly affecting employment.

Her remarks reinforce the case for additional Fed rate hikes.
(@WalterBloomberg)

TRUMP SAYS PUTIN IS READY TO END UKRAINE WAR, URGES EUROPE TO MAKE A DEAL

President Donald Trump told European leaders and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that Vladimir Putin is ready to end the war, according to five European officials briefed on Thursday's discussions.

Trump reportedly urged European governments to reach a peace agreement with Russia, arguing they could redirect spending from Ukraine toward their own countries.

No peace agreement has been announced, and Putin's willingness to end the conflict remains Trump's assessment.

TRUMP SEEKS UKRAINE PEACE DEAL BEFORE JANUARY — FT

The Trump administration wants Ukraine to reach a peace agreement with Russia by early January 2027, according to the Financial Times, citing four people briefed on the discussions.

Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner reportedly resumed negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow in Abu Dhabi, ending an eight-month pause.

The diplomatic push comes after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress, with Democrats expected to increase support for Ukraine and pressure on Russia.

No agreement has been announced.
